question: Support for companies that use the Autoroute Ferroviaire Alpine (Alpine Rolling Motorway) following the rockslide on 27 August 2023?

On 27 August 2023, a staggering 10 000 cubic metres of rock collapsed in the area of Praz, blocking the roads and railways of Haute-Maurienne in France, as well as the main border crossing point with Italy. Since then, many of the companies which use the Alpine Rolling Motorway have been at a standstill and are suffering losses of up to EUR 100 000 per month.

A large proportion of employees have already lost their jobs, and the companies still have no long-term plan. The banks are not backing them and no emergency support is being made available to these companies. If nothing is done, in a few weeks, some of them will be liquidated.

Given that the Lyon-Turin works will cost the EU billions of euros and not be completed for several years, it is imperative that we act now to help those working in the piggyback transport sector who may no longer exist when the new railway line finally sees the light of day.

Dozens of elected representatives and mayors from the area therefore support the following question: Will the Commission make EU funds available and allow state aid to save the companies that use the Alpine Rolling Motorway and are victims of the Praz rockslide?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.6.2024) The Commission acknowledges that the situation created by the landslide of rocks, around La Praz area, in August 2023, is serious and damaging for companies and their employees.

With regard to a possible State aid measure to compensate damages due to a natural disaster, please note that it is up to the Member States to decide whether they want to provide support, for public policy reasons, to a certain activity or to certain beneficiaries, the type and form of this support, as well as the amount of funding to be provided.

It is the responsibility of Member States to design the State aid measures they intend to grant and to notify the Commission of their intention. If France and/or Italy were to notify such aid, the Commission would assess it in line with the principles set out in Article 107 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

The Connecting Europe Facility funding is only available for financing of trans-European transport (TEN-T) infrastructure and cannot be used to provide a short-term relief to users of infrastructure that has suffered the damage.

Concerning potential support from the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), the agreement in place with the French authorities specifically excludes support to this kind of infrastructure and cannot be used to compensate damages due to a disaster.
